 Pakistan v Sri Lanka Second Test Prediction, Tips and Bet Builder
 Partner Authors
 Updated: 13 hours ago
 Pakistan and Sri Lanka head to Lahore for the deciding Test of their two-match series after a weather-affected draw in Rawalpindi, where both sides had moments of dominance but neither could force a result. 
 The first Test finished all square after bad light and interruptions robbed the match of significant playing time, but there was enough evidence to suggest Pakistan may have edged the contest on balance.
 Saud Shakeel continued his excellent form with the bat, debutant Saqib Khan announced himself with a remarkable seven-wicket haul, and the hosts showed plenty of resistance to bat out the final innings.
 Sri Lanka , however, will take confidence from posting 446 in their only innings, albeit the total relied heavily on centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis.
 Asitha Fernando was once again the spearhead of their attack and with the series level at 0-0 and better weather forecast for Lahore, the prospects of a result look far stronger.

 Match Prediction
 Pakistan to win @ 13/8 
 The opening Test suggested there is little between the sides, but conditions in Lahore may tilt this contest towards the hosts.
 Pakistan's batting unit looked more settled than Sri Lanka's attack during the Rawalpindi draw. Four of their top five passed fifty in the first innings and Saud Shakeel followed up with another classy knock in the second innings, falling just three runs short of a deserved century.
 Saqib Khan's emergence also gives Pakistan a genuine wicket-taking threat. His seven-wicket match haul was the standout bowling performance of the first Test and suggests Pakistan may have unearthed a bowler capable of complementing Mohammad Abbas's accuracy.
 Sri Lanka's biggest concern remains their ability to take 20 wickets. They improved significantly after a poor opening session in Rawalpindi. However, even with three specialist seamers and Milan Rathnayake acting as a fourth seamer, they struggled to apply consistent pressure for long periods.
 History also favours Pakistan. They have won four of their last six Tests against Sri Lanka, losing only one, and home advantage should prove decisive in a match likely to enjoy far fewer rain interruptions.
 Best Bet
 Salman Ali Agha Player Performance Over 78.5 @ 5/6  
 This looks an ideal opportunity for Pakistan all-rounder Salman Ali Agha to respond after enduring a disappointing start to the series.
 He was dismissed by an excellent delivery in the first innings and then fell to a stunning catch in the second.
 But Sri Lanka are the opposition against whom Salman averages highest in Test cricket and he previously produced a career-best unbeaten 132 against them.
 He could easily surpass the 78.5 player performance total here on runs alone, but he is also a useful fifth bowling option for Pakistan with his off-break deliveries, which could trouble Sri Lanka's left-handers on a turning surface. 
 And with 10 points on offer per catch taken, he could also add to his score from second slip, from where he claimed two solid catches in the first Test. 
 Series Prediction
 Pakistan to win series 1-0 
 The drawn first Test means the winner in Lahore claims the series outright and Pakistan appear slightly better equipped to seize that opportunity.
 Sri Lanka's batting showed resilience in Rawalpindi but their bowling attack still looks dependent on Asitha Fernando producing something special.
 Pakistan, by contrast, have more balance with both the bat and ball and should improve further after gaining confidence from the opening match.
 A flatter Lahore surface is also likely to suit Pakistan's stronger batting resources.
 Player Tips
 Saud Shakeel remains the most reliable performer in Pakistan's batting order and looks like an excellent option to contribute most in the hosts' first innings.
 The left-hander top-scored with 93 off 199 deliveries in the first match, showing patience and control when conditions were at their most challenging.
 He has now outperformed all Pakistan's other batters in the first innings four times in his last 13 Tests.
 The 31-year-old has an outstanding record against Sri Lanka and looks to be the standout Top Pakistan batter selection for the Lahore Test at 4/1 . 
 While Dhananjaya and Kusal Mendis weighed in with tons in the First Test, Kamindu Mendis' performance went a little under the radar.
 The left-hander played a patient 58 off 131 balls to help the visitors surpass Pakistan's first-innings total.
 Kamindu averages nearly 54 for Sri Lanka after 19 matches, and his average in Asian conditions is even more impressive at a shade under 65.
 He is 5/6 to pass his run line of 75.5 runs in Lahore.
 If the tourists are to win the contest, Asitha Fernando is likely to be central to those hopes.
 Sri Lanka's premier fast bowler reached the milestone of 100 Test wickets during the first Test and his form throughout 2026 has been outstanding.
 Fernando continually questioned Pakistan's batters in Rawalpindi and could be Sri Lanka's biggest wicket-taking threat.
 However, few debut performances have generated more excitement in recent years than Saqib Khan's display in the first Test.
 The young paceman collected seven wickets and consistently found movement, energy and discipline. 
 He is available at 1/2 to claim four or more wickets in Lahore.
